display.title: Kiddush Levanah: Blessing the New Moon Before It Wanes
display.summary_short: With one day left to bless the new moon, Uncle Yossi explains the molad, the phases of the moon, and why we say Kiddush Levanah before the moon starts to shrink.
display.summary_long: A talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, broadcast on 13 Kislev. Only one more night remains to say the blessing over the new moon. How can such an exact deadline be known for a moon more than 220,000 miles away? On Shabbos Mevarchim the time of the molad, the birth of the new moon, is announced in shul to the minute and beyond, because our Sages calculated it long in advance. Uncle Yossi explains the moon's phases: invisible at Rosh Chodesh, growing until the full moon in the middle of the month, then shrinking, which is why the brachah is said before it begins to wane. As Dovid HaMelech says, the heavens tell of Hashem's greatness, and every evening in Maariv we praise Hashem who sets the stars in their places. After about the seventh of the month people step outside after Maariv to bless the moon from the siddur. The order of the day: remind anyone who has not yet said it, so Hashem will bless us with a good month.
display.lesson: Treasure every mitzvah, even blessing the new moon, and remember that Hashem guides the whole universe in perfect order.
